sentences.text: Federal health authorities described tuberculosis control programs as having three basic objectives: the development of adequate case finding facilities in all areas of Canada, the provision of treatment measures capable of meeting the needs of every patient, and the organization of necessary rehabilitation services to assist the return of patients to normal living following treatment of the disease.

A four-fold approach to tuberculosis control was developed to include efficient case-finding, adequate treatment facilities, successful rehabilitation of the patient, and a vigorous program of prevention.

Federal funds were extensively utilized for the purchase of x-ray equipment and for the training of physicians and technicians to be engaged in the operation of x-ray, laboratory and clinical services.
Mass detection services were assisted in all provinces, with special attention being given to hospital admission x-ray examination programs and the x-raying on a regular basis of industrial groups.
Assistance was given to all provinces for the purchase of B.C.G., and federal funds were used in Quebec in the development of a large scale program of B.C.G. immunization of infants.

Rehabilitation measures were recognized as an indispensable part of any adequate tuberculosis program to prevent the relapse of arrested tuberculosis with a consequent need for repeated hospitalization.
